positioning.why_it_matters: HTML Anything matters because the agent ecosystem is moving from one-off prompts to reusable skills, instructions, and workflow packs. It gives builders a source-backed way to inspect, adapt, and compare task-specific agent capability instead of reinventing the same prompt structure every time.

core_strengths.title: Reusable skill packaging
core_strengths.description: HTML Anything treats repeated agent behavior as reusable files or workflows rather than one-off prompts.
core_strengths.why_it_matters: Reusable packaging is the difference between a clever demo and an operational agent workflow.

core_strengths.title: Source-backed adaptation
core_strengths.description: The public repository gives teams a concrete starting point for forking, pruning, and adapting skills to their own standards.
core_strengths.why_it_matters: Agent skills often need local conventions, so editable source is more valuable than a static prompt.

core_strengths.title: Useful for capability mapping
core_strengths.description: The project helps OpenAgent readers see which skill categories are emerging around coding, security, design, marketing, research, and operations.
core_strengths.why_it_matters: A good skill directory should help builders understand the shape of the ecosystem, not only collect links.
